Alex Newhook (born January 28, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Colorado Avalanche. He won the Stanley Cup in 2022 while playing for the Avalanche. Before playing in the NHL, Newhook played parts of 2 seasons with the Victoria Grizzlies of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and a year and a half with the Boston College Eagles. During his time with the Grizzlies, Newhook was awarded the Vern Dye Memorial Award for most valuable player and led the league in points. In 2020, he won the Tim Taylor Award, leading all Hockey East freshmen in both points and goals. He was the first Eagle to win the award. He was drafted 16th overall by the Colorado Avalanche in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft. On March 31, 2021, Newhook signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the Colorado Avalanche. On May 5, Newhook made his NHL debut in a 3-2 loss against the San Jose Sharks. On May 7, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Cale Makar goal in a 3-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings. On May 21, Newhook scored his first NHL goal in a 5–1 Game 3 win against the St. Louis Blues in the first round of the 2021 Stanley Cup playoffs. Newhook went on to help the Avalanche defeat the Tampa Bay Lightning 4 games to 2 in the 2022 Stanley Cup Finals to win the Stanley Cup. On June 27, 2023, the Avalanche traded Newhook to the Montreal Canadiens in exchange for prospect Gianni Fairbrother, along with a first and second round pick. On July 11, the Canadiens signed Newhook to a four-year, $11.6-million contract.

Alexander Nedeljkovic (born January 7, 1996) is an American professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the San Jose Sharks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Carolina Hurricanes, Detroit Red Wings, and Pittsburgh Penguins. Before playing in the NHL, Nedeljkovic played parts of three seasons with Plymouth Whalers, one season with the Flint Firebirds, and one season with the Niagara IceDogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the First All-Rookie Team and First All-Star Team. He was also named the OHL Goaltender of the Year and won the F. W. "Dinty" Moore Trophy for being the rookie goaltender with best goals against average. He was drafted 37th overall by the Carolina Hurricanes in the 2014 NHL entry draft. On March 27, 2015, Nedeljkovic signed a three-year, $2.25 million entry-level contract to join the Hurricanes. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Charlotte Checkers. On January 17, 2017, the Hurricanes called him up and Nedeljkovic made his NHL debut in relief of Cam Ward, stopping all 17 shots he faced in a 4–1 loss against the Columbus Blue Jackets. He was sent back down to the Checkers after the game. On March 10, 2018, Nedeljkovic was able to score a goal during a game, becoming just the 18th goaltender in AHL history to accomplish the feat. On January 23, 2019, Nedeljkovic was called back up and he made his first NHL start, stopping 24 of 26 shots he faced in a 4–1 loss against the Vancouver Canucks. On June 28, Nedeljkovic signed a three-year, $725,000 contract to stay with the Hurricanes. He helped the Checkers when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Providence Bruins, Hershey Bears, and Toronto Marlies. They went on to defeat the Chicago Wolves four games to one in the Final to win the first Calder Cup in Checkers franchise history. On February 20, 2021, Nedeljkovic stopped all 24 shots he faced to earn his first NHL shutout in a 4–0 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On July 22, 2021, the Hurricanes traded Nedeljkovic to the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for Jonathan Bernier and a 2021 third-round draft pick. The same day, Nedeljkovic signed a two-year, $6 million contract to stay with the Wings. He played parts of two seasons with the Red Wings before being sent down to their AHL-affiliate Grand Rapids Griffins. On July 1, 2023, Nedeljkovic signed a one-year, $1.5 million contract to join the Pittsburgh Penguins. On June 20, 2024, Nedeljkovic signed a two-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Penguins. On July 1, 2025, the Penguins traded Nedeljkovic to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for a 2028 third-round draft pick. On March 6, 2026, Nedeljkovic signed a two-year, $6 million contract to stay with the Sharks.

Alex Laferriere (born October 28, 2001) is an American professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Laferriere played three seasons with the Des Moines Buccaneers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Harvard Crimson of ECAC Hockey. He was drafted 83rd overall by the Los Angeles Kings in the 2014 NHL entry draft. On April 9, 2023, Laferriere signed a three-year, $2.4 million entry-level contract to join the Hurricanes. He was sent down to their AHL-affiliate Ontario Reign. On October 11, 2023, the Kings called him up and Laferriere made his NHL debut in a 5–2 loss against the Colorado Avalanche. On October 21, Laferriere scored his first NHL goal against Jeremy Swayman in a 4–1 win against the Boston Bruins. On August 2, 2025, Laferriere signed a three-year, $12.3 million contract to stay with the Kings.

Alexander Petrovic (born March 3, 1992) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Edmonton Oilers and Dallas Stars. Before playing in the NHL, Petrovic played five seasons with the Red Deer Rebels of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Rebels. He was named to the East Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 36th overall by the Florida Panthers of the 2010 NHL entry draft. On March 2, 2025, Petrovic signed an three-year, $2.475 million entry-level contract to join the Panthers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates San Antonio Rampage. On April 18, 2013, the Panthers called him up and Petrovic made his NHL debut in a 6–1 loss against the New York Rangers. On March 13, 2014, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Brandon Pirri goal in a 5–4 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On July 15, 2015, Petrovic signed a two-year, $2.1 million contract to stay with the Panthers. On January 26, 2016, Petrovic scored his first NHL goal against James Reimer in a 5–1 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On June 30, 2017, Petrovic signed a one-year, $1.85 million contract to stay with the Panthers. On July 6, 2018, Petrovic signed a one-year contract to stay with the Panthers. On December 30, 2018, the Panthers traded Petrovic to his hometown Edmonton Oilers in exchange for Chris Wideman and a 2019 conditional third-round draft pick. He recorded one assist in 9 regular season games for the Oilers. On September 26, 2019, Petrovic signed a one-year contract to join the Boston Bruins. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Providence Bruins. He scored 2 goals and recorded 18 assists in 54 regular season games for Providence. He never played for Boston. On October 9, 2020, Petrovic signed a one-year contract to join the Calgary Flames. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Stockton Heat. He scored 2 goals and recorded 10 assists in 17 regular season games for the Heat. He never played for the Flames. On July 28, 2021, Petrovic signed a one-year contract to join the Dallas Stars. On June 7, 2022, Petrovic signed a one-year contract to stay with the Stars. On June 7, 2023, Petrovic signed a one-year contract to stay with the Stars. On July 1, 2026, Petrovic signed a two-year, $1.75 million contract to rejoin the Florida Panthers.

Alexander Robertson "Duke" Wellington (August 4, 1893 – September 20, 1967) was a Canadian professional ice hockey player. Wellington played senior ice hockey and one game in the National Hockey League for the Quebec Bulldogs during the 1919–20 NHL season.

Alexander Smart (May 29, 1918 – April 18, 2005) was a Canadian ice hockey forward. He played one season for the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League and spent the majority of his career in the Quebec Senior Hockey League. Born in Brandon, Manitoba, Smart played junior hockey in the Manitoba Junior Hockey League with the Portage Terriers for two seasons. In 1937–38, joined the senior ranks with the Toronto Marlboros of the Ontario Hockey Association and scored 23 points in 12 games at a goal-per-game pace. The following season, he began a three-year stint in the Montreal City Hockey League (MCHL) with the Verdun Maple Leafs and Montreal Sr. Canadiens. In 1941–42, Smart moved with the Sr. Canadiens to the Quebec Senior Hockey League (QSHL). Affiliated with the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League, Smart was called up to the NHL in 1943 and, on January 14, became the first player in league history to score a hat trick in his NHL debut (this feat was later matched by Réal Cloutier of the Quebec Nordiques in 1979, Fabian Brunnström of the Dallas Stars in 2008, and Derek Stepan of the New York Rangers in 2010). He completed the season with 5 goals and 2 assists in 8 games – the lone NHL stint of his career. Smart spent the remainder of his career in the QSHL with the Montreal Royals and Ottawa Senators with the exception of one more season in the MCHL with the Montreal Vickers and the final season of his career in the OVHL with Eastview St. Charles. He recorded a career-high 66 points in 47 games with the Senators in 1947–48, then helped the club to an Allan Cup in 1949 as Canada's senior amateur champions. Smart retired after the 1950–51 season spent with Eastview.

Alexis Cabrera (née Kaufman, born August 9, 1991), better known by her ring name Alexa Bliss, is an American professional wrestler. She is currently signed to WWE and performs on their SmackDown brand. Cabrera signed a contract with WWE in May 2013. She trained at the WWE Performance Center. She first performed as Alexa Bliss for WWE NXT. In July 2016 Bliss was moved to WWE SmackDown where she won the SmackDown Women's Championship two times, and is the first person to win it twice. She moved to Raw in April 2017. She won the Raw Women's Championship later that month. She would go on to win it three times. Bliss was the first person to win both the SmackDown and Raw Women's championships. Cabrera said that watching Trish Stratus and Rey Mysterio got her into wrestling. She is a big fan of Disney, when she was younger her family went to Walt Disney World each year. She also supports her hometown ice hockey team the Columbus Blue Jackets. Cabrera was engaged to another wrestler Matthew Adams, who is better known by his ring name Buddy Murphy. In 2022 she married singer Ryan Cabrera. On November 27, 2023, they welcomed their daughter, Hendrix Rouge Cabrera. Alexander Stalock (born July 28, 1987, Minnesota) is an American sports commentator and former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played parts of eleven seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the San Jose Sharks, Minnesota Wild, and Chicago Blackhawks. After retiring, he became a sports color commentator for the San Jose Sharks. Before playing in the NHL, Stalock played two seasons with Cedar Rapids RoughRiders of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Minnesota Duluth Bulldogs of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). During his time with the RoughRiders, Stalock helped the team win the Clark Cup and was named as both the USHL Playoff MVP and USHL Goaltender of the Year. During his time with the Bulldogs, Stalock helped the team reach the Final Five championship. He was also named to the 2007 WCHA All-Rookie Team, and to the 2009 NCAA West First All-American Team and WCHA First All-Star Team. He was drafted 112th overall by the San Jose Sharks in the 2005 NHL entry draft. He spent two seasons playing for San Jose's AHL-affiliate Worcester Sharks. During his time in Worcester, he set an AHL record for wins by a rookie with 39. On February 1, 2011, the Sharks called Stalock up and he made his NHL debut in a 5–3 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes, earning his first NHL win in the process. After the game, he was sent back down to the AHL. He suffered a season-ending injury after Dwight King stepped on his knee and sliced his nerve. On July 10, 2013, Stalock signed a one-year contract to remain with the Sharks. On October 27, Stalock made his first career NHL start in a 5–2 win against the Ottawa Senators. On January 16, 2014, Stalock recorded his first NHL shutout in a 3–0 win against the Florida Panthers. On February 27, 2016, the Sharks traded Stalock along with Ben Smith and a 2018 conditional fourth-round pick to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for James Reimer and Jeremy Morin. He never played a game with them and was immediately waived, sending him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Toronto Marlies. He played 3 games with them. On July 1, 2016, Stalock signed a one-year, two-way contract with the Minnesota Wild. He spent the season playing for their AHL-affiliate Iowa Wild. On February 2, 2017, Stalock signed a two-year, $1.3 million extension to stay with the Wild. On December 6, 2018, he played in a 2–0 loss to the Calgary Flames, it was his 100th game in the NHL. On January 29, 2019, he signed a three-year, $2.355 million extension to stay with the Wild. On March 1, 2021, Stalock was picked up off waiver by the Edmonton Oilers. He did not play for the team because he was out with myocarditis after contracting COVID-19. On March 2, 2022, the Oilers traded Stalock to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for future considerations. He only played one game with the Sharks before being sent down to their AHL-affiliate, San Jose Barracuda. On July 13, 2022, Stalock signed a one-year contract to join the Chicago Blackhawks. He played 27 games with them and was a finalist for the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy. On August 7, 2023, Stalock signed a one-year, $800,000 contract with the Anaheim Ducks but never played a game with them. In 2024, Stalock announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey and joining the San Jose Sharks as a radio color commentator.

Alex Sánchez Cruz (July 20, 1930 – December 5, 2025) was a Costa Rican footballer. He started playing as a goalkeeper in the youth team of Deportivo Saprissa, before moving to wing-back at Orión. He played mostly for Deportivo Saprissa and Alajuelense, and won three league titles with Saprissa. He was capped 32 times for Costa Rica between 1950 and 1963, making his debut at the 1950 Central American and Caribbean Games. He would later play for them at the 1951 Pan American Games, where Costa Rica won a silver medal. In October 1957, he played in two 1958 FIFA World Cup qualification matches against Mexico. Sánchez died on December 5, 2025, at the age of 95. Silver medalist at the 1951 Pan American Games

Alex Vlasic (born June 5, 2001) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Vlasic played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Boston University Terriers of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. He scored 1 goal and recorded 7 assists for 8 points and was named a Hockey East All-Star for his efforts. He was drafted 43rd overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2019 NHL entry draft. On March 15, 2022, Vlasic signed a three-year, $916,667 entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. On December 13, 2025, Vlasic made his NHL debut in a 3–1 loss against the Minnesota Wild. On April 20, Vlasic scored his first NHL goal against Karel Vejmelka in a 4–3 win against the Arizona Coyotes. On April 25, 2024, Vlasic signed a six-year, $27.6 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. Vlasic's older cousin Marc-Édouard also played in the NHL for 19 seasons in the NHL for the San Jose Sharks. his older sister Emma is also a professional ice hockey player. When he was 13 years old, Vlasic was diagnosed with celiac disease.

Alex Zanardi was an Italian racing driver, cyclist and Paralympic gold medalist. In 2001, Zanardi was racing in the IndyCar race at eurospeedway and was involved in an wreck which severed both of his legs.

Alex Turcotte (born February 26, 2001) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Turcotte played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one year with Denver Pioneers of National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He was drafted 5th overall by the Los Angeles Kings in the 2019 NHL entry draft. On March 11, 2020, Turcotte signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Kings. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Ontario Reign. On December 28, 2021, the Kings called him up and Turcotte made his NHL debut in a 6–3 loss against the Vegas Golden Knights. On January 31, 2024, he scored his first NHL goal against Juuse Saros and also recorded an assist from of a Trevor Lewis goal in a 4–2 win against the Nashville Predators. On January 13, 2019, Turcotte signed a two-year, $1.55 million contract to stay with the Kings. On June 22, 2024, Turcotte signed a three-year contract to stay with the Kings. Turcotte's father Alfie Turcotte was also a professional hockey player and played seven seasons in the NHL.

Alexander Andrijevski (born August 10, 1968 in Minsk, Belarus) is a Belarusian former professional ice hockey right winger who played one game for the Chicago Blackhawks in the National Hockey League (NHL).

Alexander Alexandrovich Belov, commonly known as Sasha Belov (November 9, 1951 – October 3, 1978) was a Soviet basketball player. He played at the center position. Then he was assistance coach in the youth department of Salzburg. 2020/21 he was assistance coach to Mathias Jaissle with FC Liefering. On July 1st,2021 he followed Jaissle to FC Red Bull Salzburg as assistance coach.

Alexander Gabriel Holtz (born 23 January 2002) is a Swedish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New Jersey Devils. Outside of the NHL, Holtz played for Djurgårdens IF of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Holtz played parts of three seasons with Djurgårdens IF of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He was drafted 7th overall by the New Jersey Devils in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On 19 April 2021, Holtz signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Devils. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Binghamton Devils and Utica Comets. On 5 November 2021, the Devils called him up and Holtz made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On 9 November, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Pavel Zacha goal in a 7–3 win against the Florida Panthers. On 13 October 2022, Holtz scored his first NHL goal against Carter Hart in a 5–2 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers. On 8 March 2024, the Devils traded Holtz along with Akira Schmid to the Vegas Golden Knights in exchange for Paul Cotter and a 2025 third-round draft pick. On 7 October 2025, Holtz signed an two-year, $837,500 contract to stay with the Knights.

Alexander Mikhaylovich Ovechkin (born September 17, 1985) is a Russian professional ice hockey left winger. He plays for the Washington Capitals of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as their captain. Ovechkin was picked first overall in the 2004 NHL Entry Draft. He also played for the Dynamo Moscow of the RSL from 2001 to 2005 and again in 2012 because of the 2012-13 NHL lockout.

Alexander Gennadevitch Mogilny (born February 18, 1969) is a Russian retired professional ice hockey right winger. He played 17 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) with the Buffalo Sabres, New Jersey Devils, Toronto Maple Leafs and Vancouver Canucks organizations. He won a gold medal at the 1988 Winter Olympics with the Soviet Union hockey team. He won a Stanley Cup in 2000 with the Devils. He was named a member of the Buffalo Sabres Hall of Fame on January 1, 2011.

Alexander Münninghoff (13 April 1944 – 28 April 2020) was a Polish-born Dutch journalist and chess player. From 1974 to 2007, he worked for the Haagsche Courant. Münninghoff wrote among others many articles and books about chess sport. He was born in Poznan, Poland. In 1983 he won the and in 2015 he won the for his book De stamhouder. Münninghoff died at his home in The Hague on 28 April 2020, aged 76.

Alexander Socrates Onassis (; April 30, 1948January 23, 1973) was an American-born Greek businessman. He was the son of the Greek shipping magnate Aristotle Onassis and his first wife Tina Livanos. He and his sister Christina Onassis were upset by his father's marriage to Jacqueline Kennedy. He was the head of Olympic Aviation, a Greek airline owned by his father. Onassis died in hospital as a result of injuries from an airplane crash at Hellinikon International Airport at the age of 24.

Alexander McDonnell (born on 1798–1835) was an Irish chess master. who played in a competition, a series with six matches with the world's leading Chess Player Louis-Charles Mahé de La Bourdonnais in 1834

Alexander Prass (born 26 May 2001) is an Austrian professional footballer. He plays as a midfielder for Austrian Football Bundesliga club Sturm Graz and the Austria U21 national team. He started his career with LASK and FC Pasching. 2012 he went to FC Red Bull Salzburg where he played in the youth and the Red Bull Salzburg Academy. 2019 he went on to FC Liefering. He debuted on March 8th, 2019 versus Young Violets Austria Wien. In two and a half seasons he played 59 matches for Liefering and scored 12 goals. On 28 May 2021, he signed a three-year contract with Sturm Graz. In early August 2024, Prass moved to Bundesliga club TSG 1899 Hoffenheim. He debuted on October 9th 2018 for the Austrian U18 team versus Switzerland. On October, 11th he scored his first goal. October 2019 he debuted for the U19 team and in March 2021 he played his first match for the U21 team versus Saudi Arabia. In November 2022, he was first called up to the senior national team. In the same month, he made his debut for the national team against Andorra. In May 2024, he was named to Austria's preliminary squad for Euro 2024. He finally was part of the UEFA Euro squad. He played in all four of Austria's tournament matches. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Prass goal.

Alexander Neufeld- Nemes (25 September 1899 – 27 October 1977) ( also known as Sandor Nemes) was a Hungarian football player and manager. He played in Hungary, Austria, Switzerland, United States and Yugoslavia. He played for the national teams of Hungary and Austria. He was born in Budapest to a Jewish family. Neufeld started playing football for a local club named ILK. 1916 he joined Ferencvárosi TC Due to his skills he got promoted to the senior squad. At first he played as striker but s changed his position to right-winger. In both 1918 and 1919 they finished second in the Hungarian Championship behind the then dominating MTK Budapest. With Ferencváros he played a total of 57 league matches having scored 18 goals Due to the political situation after the First World War many Hungarian players left the country. Neufeld signed with second league Austrian club SC Hakoah Vienna. He played his first match with Hakoah in November 1919 and became soon one of the most important players in their aspiration to get promotion to the first league. The Hungarian Football Federation had a confrontation with Austrian clubs over the players that begin playing for Austrian clubs without being officially released from their origin clubs in Hungary. Until the end of 1919 these players, among the Neufeld, were not allowed to play. This situation lasted until March 1920 when all players were allowed to play again. In his first season with Hakoah he reached the semi-finals of theAustrian Cup. 1920 Nemes went back to Ferencváros as they played in Switzerland. He decided to stay in Switzerland and went to FC Basel, Nemes played only one month with the team in two test games. He received an invitation from the German businessman Otto Eidinger to participate in a newly formed Hungarian professional team. He planed to play exhibition matches all over Europe. Neufeld accepted the invitation along with a number of other notable players. After only a few weeks it was stopped with players complaining about not being paid. Most of the players returned to Austria and Hungary. They were sanctioned by the federations.Nemes received a suspension to last until April 1921. He moved to Czechoslovakia and signed with Maccabi Brno. Soon afterwards an agreement was reached about an amnesty for players that would accept to return. Nemes returned to Hakoah in summer 1921 and became part of Hakoah team that this time played in the Austrian Bundesliga. In his first complete season in 1921–22 Hakoah finished second in the league. In the next season Hakoah finished in mid table. Neufeld scored 16 goals and finishing in third place as league top scorer. In 1924 Hakoah won the first professional Austrian championship. By then, Nemes had already played four times with the city selection of Vienna, and Austria national team manager Hugo Meisl convoked him for the match on 5 July 1925, in Stockholm against Sweden, where he made his debut for the Austria national football team in the 4–2 win. He will play his second match for Austria on 8 November, that same year, in a 0–2 loss against Switzerland in Bern. He played both matches under the name of Alexander Neufeld. In spring 1926 Hakoah made a successful tournée in the United States. Nemes returned to Austria and finished that season. He informed the club that at the end of the season he will leave Hakoah and move to the United States by accepting the offer of Brooklyn Wanderers. After one season in America, Nemes returned to Hakoah. Nemes returned to the States in 1929 and played with Hakoah All-Stars until 1930. In fall of 1930 he played with Fall River F.C. helping them to win the 1930 American Soccer League. He finished his player career with BSK Belgrade in the Yugoslav Championship and Alexandria in Egypt. On 12 May 1918 he made his debut for the Hungarian national team playing in attack along Alfred Schaffer and Imre Schlosser in the 2–1 win over Switzerland in Budapest. A few weeks later, on 2 June, in Vienna, he played again this time winning Austria by 2–0. On 5 October 1919, he played his third match for the Hungarian national team, again in Vienna against Austria, however this time they were defeated by 0–2. He played his first match for the Austrian national football team on 5 July 1925, in Stockholm against Sweden in the 4–2 win. His second and last match for Austria was on 8 November in a 0–2 loss against Switzerland in Bern. In 1930 Nemes moved to the Kingdom of Yugoslavia He became coach of one of the strongest clubs in the country BSK Belgrade and soon he makes his first major coaching success by winning the 1930–31 Yugoslav Championship. Then he returned to Austria in 1931 and worked one season as coach with a Second league Jewish club named Hasmonea. After that he returned to BSK. 1935 he went to Hapoel Hatzair in Palestina. 1936 he returned to Belgrade where he will win another championship in 1939. Afterwards he had a brief spell coaching Turkish Galatasaray Then he went back to Israel in 1950 to coach Hapoel Tel Aviv. His real name is Sándor Nemes. For unknown reasons he begin to be known by the mid-1920s as Alexander Neufeld. Fall River F.C. Yugoslav Championship (4): 1931, 1933, 1936, 1939

Alexander Douglas Kerfoot (born August 11, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Utah Mammoth of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as an alternate captain. He has also played for the Colorado Avalanche, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Arizona Coyotes. Before playing in the NHL, Kerfoot played parts of 3 seasons with the Coquitlam Express of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and four years at Harvard with the Crimson. During his time with the Express, Kerfoot would win the Bob Fenton Trophy as the most sportsmanlike player in the league. He would also be named to the All-Rookie and All-Star teams. While playing with Harvard, Kerfoot would be named to the Second All-Ivy Team and earned a spot in the ECAC Third All-Star Team after recording 30 assists in his 2015–16 junior year. He was drafted 150th overall by the New Jersey Devils in the 2012 NHL Entry Draft. Kerfoot decided not to play for them and instead play at Harvard. After his time at Harvard was done, he became a free agent. On August 23, 2017, Kerfoot signed a two-year; entry level contract with the Colorado Avalanche. On October 5, Kerfoot made his NHL debut. He would also record his first NHL point in the same game when assisted on a Tyson Barrie goal in a 4-2 win against the New York Rangers. On October 11, he would score his first NHL goal in a 6-3 season opening win against the Boston Bruins. On July 1, 2019, the Avalanche would trade Kerfoot, Tyson Barrie and a sixth-round pick to the Toronto Maple Leafs for Nazem Kadri, Calle Rosén and a third-round pick. He would sign a four-year, $14 million contract with the Maple Leafs three days later. He would play four seasons with them. On July 1, 2023, Kerfoot signed a two-year, $7 million contract with the Arizona Coyotes as a free agent. After the 2023–24 regular season ended, the Arizona Coyotes would be suspended and the team moved to Utah to become the Utah Hockey Club. Kerfoot would move along with the team.

Alexander Popovich (born 18 July 1891 in Vienna; died 7 September 1952 in Vienna) was an Austrian football player and coach. The defender was the first Austrian footballer to reach 30 international caps. Popovich began his career as a youth player at Wiener AC. He quickly rose to the reserve team. When a promised appearance in the first team failed, he left the club and joined Viktoria, where he played for a year before moving to the Vienna Cricket and Football Club. At that time he was still playing as a winger, but the Cricketers soon recognized his talent as a defender. In 1910 he became one of the founding members of Wiener Amateur SV and quickly became a regular starter for the new club. He played continuously in the First Division until 1922. In 1920, he commuted between Vienna and Prague, playing simultaneously for the Amateurs and DFC Prague. Successes came towards the end of his career. He won the Cup with the Amateurs. In the 1922-23 season he became champion with SK Rapid Wien. 1923-24 he won the double with Amateur SV. Although he only played for a smaller club, Popovich became one of the long-serving pillars of the Austrian national team. From his debut on 10 September 1911, in a 2-1 victory over Germany, he played a then-remarkable 33 international matches until 1923. His last match was a 2-4 loss versus Sweden on 10 June 1923. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Pesser goal. The defender ended his career at WAC. He went to Berlin to Hertha BSC. He became German runner-up as coach in 1927. Then he coached SC Minerva 1893. From 1941 to 1943 he coached Lazio Rome. In the 1945/46 season he was coach of FC Bologna and later AC Pro Sesto. In the 1910s and 1920s, he was active as an ice hockey goalkeeper alongside football. He played for Wiener Eislauf-Verein, with whom he won numerous championships.

Alexander Murillo Albert (born 4 October 2006) is a Spanish professional footballer. He plays as a forward for Austrian 2. Liga team FC Liefering. Murillo was born in Alicante, Spain, to Colombian parents. He is the nephew of former Once Caldas player Jairo Murillo. Murillo began his career in the academy of Kelme CF. He joined the academy of Austrian Bundesliga club Red Bull Salzburg in January 2023. He made his debut for FC Liefering in the Austrian 2. Liga in October 2024, when he came on as a substitute for Tim Paumgartner in the 87th minute against Floridsdorfer AC. Murillo played two friendly matches for Spain's under-16 team against Switzerland. He can still play for Colombia in international football.

Alexander Alexandrovich Nikishin (; born 2 October 2001) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Carolina Hurricanes of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Nikishin played for Spartak Moscow and SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Nikishin is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Hurricanes in 2026. Internationally, Nikishin plays for the Russian Olympic Committee and won a silver medal with the ROC in 2022. Before playing in the NHL, Nikishin played parts of three seasons with Spartak Moscow and three seasons with SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 69th overall by the Carolina Hurricanes in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On 11 April 2025, Nikishin signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Hurricanes. During game 5 of the Eastern conference second round on 15 May 2025, Nikishin made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the Washington Capitals. During game 4 of the East conference finals on 26 May, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Logan Stankoven goal in a 3–1 win against the Washington Capitals. On 16 October, Nikishin scored his first NHL goal against Lukáš Dostál in a 4–1 win against the Anaheim Ducks. He helped the Hurricanes during the playoffs. They defeated the Ottawa Senators, Philadelphia Flyers, and Montreal Canadiens. They went on to defeat the Vegas Golden Knights four games to two in the Final to win the Stanley Cup.

Alexander Urbom (born December 20, 1990) is a Swedish professional ice hockey defenceman who is currently playing for EC Red Bull Salzburg of the ICE Hockey League (ICEHL). He has also played for New Jersey Devils and Washington Capitals in the National Hockey League (NHL), with Djurgårdens IF and Skellefteå AIK in the Elitserien/Swedish Hockey League (SEL/SHL), Severstal Cherepovets of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL), and Düsseldorfer EG of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). He was drafted by the New Jersey Devils in the third round, 73rd overall, in the 2009 NHL Draft.

Alexander Sulzer (born May 30, 1984) is a German professional ice hockey defenceman currently playing for Düsseldorfer EG of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). Sulzer has also played in the NHL for the Nashville Predators, Florida Panthers, Vancouver Canucks, Buffalo Sabres and the DEL for the Hamburg Freezers and DEG Metro Stars. He was traded to the Florida Panthers on February 25, 2011 for a conditional draft pick in the 2011 NHL Draft.

Alexander Salák (born January 5, 1987) is a Czech professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for SKA Saint Petersburg in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Salák started his career playing in the SM-liiga with the TPS Turku. He played there for 2 seasons and was signed by the Florida Panthers of the NHL on May 29, 2009. He played two games with the Panthers and was sent down to their AHL affiliate, the Rochester Americans. Salák was loaned to Färjestads BK of the Swedish Elite League (SEL) to play in the 2010-11 season. On February 9, 2011, the Panthers traded Salák along with Michael Frolík to the Chicago Blackhawks for Jack Skille, Hugh Jessiman, and David Pacan. The Blackhawks signed him to a two-year contract on May 31, 2011. The Blackhawks released him from his contract on June 18, 2012.

Alexander Schlager (born 1 February 1996) is an Austrian professional footballer. He plays as goalkeeper for Austrian Bundesliga club FC Red Bull Salzburg and the Austria national team. Schlager began his career at ASK Salzburg. He then moved to FC Red Bull Salzburg. From April to August 2007 he played in the youth team of ASK Maxglan. In August 2007 he moved to SV Austria Salzburg. In 2009 he returned to the youth team of Red Bull Salzburg. He played then for the Red Bull Salzburg academy. In May 2012 he made his debut for the Red Bull Salzburg Juniors in the Regionalliga West. He was in the stgarting team. But this was his only appearance for the Red Bull Juniors. In May 2013, he made his debut in Salzburg's professional squad against FK Austria Wien, but did not play. For the 2014–15 season he was loaned to Germany to the A-Juniors of RB Leipzig. In October 2014 he made his first appearance in the A-Junior Bundesliga against Dynamo Dresden. In November 2014 he was in the squad for the fifth-rate second team in Leipzig for the first time against the second team of FC Carl Zeiss Jena, but was not used. By the end of the season he had played 18 games in the A-Junior Bundesliga. Leipzig became champion of the North/Northeast season. In the relegetion round they failed in the semifinals at TSG 1899 Hoffenheim. For the 2015–16 season he was loaned to Bundesliga club SV Grödig. He made his Bundesliga debut for Grödig in July 2015 when he started against SCR Altach. During his loan, he made ten Bundesliga appearances for SV Grödig. They were relegated from the Bundesliga at the end of the season. For the 2016–17 season Schlager moved to the second division club Floridsdorfer AC. In July 2016 he played his first game in the second division against WSG Wattens. By the end of the season he had made 23 appearances for Floridsdorf. For the 2017–18 season he went to Bundesliga club LASK. In his first season he was behind Pavao Pervan. So he only played one match for LASK in the Bundesliga. After Pervan left, Schlager became LASK's first goalkeeper in the summer of 2018 and also played his first international competition at club level against Lillestrøm SK. In September 2018, his contract was extended until June 2021. In the 2018–19 season he made 31 Bundesliga appearances and finished runners-up with LASK. In December 2022, LASK announced that Schlager leave LASK after the 2022–23 season. He then returned to Red Bull Salzburg for the 2023/24 season and signed till June 2027. He played for Austria U-21 and also the other youth teams from U16 to U19. He was the captain for Austria U-21 in Euro U-21 2019. On 16 November 2019, Schlager played his first match for Austria's national team in the deciding UEFA Euro 2020 qualifier against North Macedonia in Vienna.

Alexander Sean Pablo Robertson (born 17 April 2003) is a Scottish-born Australian soccer player. He plays for Portsmouth in the EFL League One and for the Australia men's national soccer team (nicknamed the "Socceroos").

Alexander Schmidt (born January 19, 1998 in Vienna) is an Austrian football player. He plays as forward for the Austrian Football Bundesliga club FC Blau-Weiß Linz. Schmidt began his career at First Vienna FC. In 2012 he moved to the FC Red Bull Salzburg academy. In the summer of 2016 he became part of the FC Liefering squad in the 2nd league. He made his debut in the second division in November 2016. He came on as a substitute for Robert Mudražija versus SC Austria Lustenau. For FC Red Bull Salzburg he was in the U-19 team for the UEFA Youth League. In the final game he scored the winning goal against Benfica. In December 2017, his contract was extended until May 2021. For the 2019/20 season he was loaned to the Bundesliga club Wolfsberger AC. For the 2020/21 season he moved to LASK. However, Schmidt was loaned directly to league rivals SKN St. Pölten. With the SKN he was relegated from the Bundesliga at the end of the season. He returned to LASK for the 2021/22 season. In September 2022, Schmidt moved to Portugal to FC Vizela. He then returned to Austria and moved to FK Austria Wien. He made 18 Bundesliga appearances for Austria. For the 2024/25 season he then moved on within the league to FC Blau-Weiß Linz. Schmidt played for the Austrian U-17 team for the first time in February 2015 against Italy. In November 2019 he made his debut for the U-21 team against Kosovo.

Alexander Stanislavovich Romanov (; born 6 January 2000) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the New York Islanders of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Montreal Canadiens. Outside of the NHL, Romanov played for CSKA Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Romanov is a one-time Gagarin Cup champion, winning with CSKA in 2019. Before playing in the NHL, Romanov played two seasons with CSKA Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He had a successful time with CSKA. He helped them during playoffs. They defeated the HC Vityaz, HC Dynamo Moscow, and SKA Saint Petersburg. They went on to defeat the Avangard Omsk four games to zero in the Final to win the first Gagarin Cup in SKA franchise history. He was drafted 38th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 2018 NHL entry draft. On 13 July 2020, Romanov signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Canadiens. On 13 January 2021, Romanov made his NHL debut in a 5–4 overtime loss against the Toronto Maple Leafs. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Tomáš Tatar goal. On 18 January, Romanov scored his first NHL goal against Mikko Koskinen in a 3–1 win against the Edmonton Oilers. On 7 July 2022, the Canadiens traded Romanov along with a 2022 fourth-round draft pick to the New York Islanders in exchange for a 2022 first-round draft pick. On 22 August, Romanov signed a three-year, $7.5 million contract to stay with the Islanders. On 30 June 2025, Romanov signed a eight-year, $50 million contract to stay with the Islanders. Romanov's maternal grandfather Zinetula Bilyaletdinov was also a professional hockey player who won a gold and silver medal with the Soviet Union.

Alexander "Alex" Zickler (born 28 February 1974 in Bad Salzungen, then German Democratic Republic) is a German football manager and former football player. He played as a striker. During his career he played for FC Bayern Munich. He started playing at the age of six with Dynamo Dresden. He played in all youth ranks. His debut in the first team was on 23 October 1992 against 1. FC Nuremberg. In July 1993 Zickler went to FC Bayern Munich where he stayed as a player for 11 seasons. During this time he was often injured. He scored 18 goals as substitute which is record in the German Bundesliga. In June 2005 he went to FC Red Bull Salzburg together with his teammate Thomas Linke. With Red Bull Salzburg he won three Austrian titles. 2006 he was elected Austrian footballer of the year by the coaches of the Austrian Bundesliga. 2010 he went to LASK Linz. After the end of the 2010/11 season he retired from football. He went back to Red Bull Salzburg where he works as contact partner for fans and partner firms. Alexander Zickler played 17 times for Germanys U21 national team and scored 7 goals. In 12 matches for the German national football team he scored two goals. Bundesliga (7): 1993–94, 1996–97, 1998–99, 1999–2000, 2000–01, 2002–03, 2004–05 DFB-Pokal (4): 1997–98, 1999–2000, 2002–03, 2004–05 DFB-Ligapokal (5): 1996–97, 1997–98, 1998–99, 1999–2000, 2003–04 Austrian Bundesliga (3): 2006–07, 2008–09, 2009–10 Austrian League Topscorer (2): 2006-07, 2007–08 Austrian Footballer of the Year (1): 2005–06 Austrian Footballers Association Player of the Year (1): 2006–07

Alexander Vladimirovich Volkov (; 3 March 1967 – 19 October 2019) was a Russian professional tennis player. He was born in Kaliningrad, Soviet Union. Volkov won his first top-level professional singles title in 1991 at Milan. At Wimbledon that year, he lost a close match in the fourth round to the eventual tournament champion Michael Stich. Volkov died on 19 October 2019 in Kalinigrad at the age of 52.

Alexander Wennberg (born 22 September 1994) is a Swedish professional ice hockey player. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He used to play for the Columbus Blue Jackets and Florida Panthers.

Alexandra Frantseva (born 24 April 1987) is a skier from Russia. She has a disability: she cannot see everything. She skied at the 2011 IPC Alpine Skiing World Championships. She was the second skier to finish in the women's visually impaired Super-G race, Giant slalom race and Super Combined race, and the third skier to finish the women's visually impaired downhill race and slalom race. Because she cannot see, Evgenia Kolosovskaya was her guide and told her where to go when going down the mountain.

Alexandra Jasmine Myles (born 17 October 1990) is a New Zealand water polo player. She is a member of the New Zealand women's national water polo team. She played at the 2009 World Aquatics Championships, 2011 World Aquatics Championships, and 2013 World Aquatics Championships.

Alexandra Rose Boyd (born 8 July 1991) is a New Zealand water polo player and coach. She is a member of the New Zealand women's national water polo team. She played at the 2011 World Aquatics Championships, and 2016 Olympic Qualification Tournament, and 2017 World Aquatics Championships.

Alexandra Schilling (born 9 November 1981) is a German female water polo player. She was part of the Germany women's national water polo team at the 2009 Women's Water Polo World League, and 2009 World Aquatics Championships.

Alexandra Coletti (born 8 August 1983 in La Colle, Monaco) is an alpine skier. She went to the 2006 Winter Olympics and the 2010 Winter Olympics for Monaco. She was Monaco's flagbearer at the Opening Ceremony of the 2010 Winter Olympics. She also won the silver medal at the 2005 European Cup for downhill skiing. Her brother, Stefano Coletti, is a racing driver in the IndyCar Series.

Alexandra Maniego Eala (born May 23, 2005) is a Filipino professional tennis player. On August 24, 2026, she achieved a career-high singles ranking of world No. 18, the highest ever for a Filipino and Southeast Asian in WTA Tour history. She is the first Filipino to break into the top 20, defeat top-10 opponents, reach the fourth round of a major, reach the semifinals of a WTA 1000 event, and win a WTA Tour title, clinching her breakthrough at the 2026 Washington Open. Eala reached a junior combined ranking of world No. 2 on October 6, 2020, and became the first Filipino to win a junior major title, winning the girls' singles title at the 2022 US Open. Alexandra Maniego Eala was born on May 23, 2005, in Quezon City, Philippines. Her father was Michael Eala, a business executive. Her mother was Rosemarie "Rizza" Maniego-Eala, former Globe Telecom CFO and SEA Games swimming medalist. She is the niece of sports official Noli Eala. Her brother Michael "Miko" Eala played tennis for Pennsylvania State University. Eala started tennis at age four. She was coached by her grandfather Roberto "Bobby" Maniego. She later studied at Immaculate Conception Academy and Colegio San Agustin – Makati. Later she trained at the Rafa Nadal Academy in Spain, where she graduated in 2023. At twelve, Eala won the Les Petits As title in France. Later she won junior doubles titles at the 2020 Australian Open with Priska Nugroho and the 2021 French Open with Oksana Selekhmeteva. She made history with the 2022 US Open girls’ singles crown, the Philippines’ first junior Grand Slam singles win. Eala turned professional in 2020. She started on the ITF Women’s Circuit in Spain and Tunisia. In 2021, she won her first singles title at ITF W15 Manacor, earning recognition from Rafael Nadal. In 2022, she added another singles crown at ITF W25 Chiang Rai. She reached the finals and semifinals at W60 Madrid and Vitoria-Gasteiz. In 2023, Eala won ITF W15 Yecla and ITF W25 Roehampton. She also entered the qualifying draw of the Australian Open, marking her first attempt at a Grand Slam event. In 2024, she claimed her biggest ITF singles crown at the W100 Vitoria-Gasteiz. She won three doubles titles. She continued to compete in qualifiers across the Grand Slam circuit. Her breakthrough came in 2025 on the WTA Tour. Eala reached the Miami Open semifinal against Jessica Pegula. She played the Eastbourne Open final. She won her first WTA125 singles title at Guadalajara. She made her Grand Slam main-draw debut, advancing to the second round in doubles at the French Open, and later reached the second round of the US Open, her best result to date. In 2026, Eala reached the semifinals in singles and doubles at the ASB Classic in Auckland, the doubles semifinals and singles quarterfinals at the Abu Dhabi Open, and quarterfinals at the WTA125 Philippine Women’s Open and Dubai Tennis Championships. She competed in the main draw of the Australian Open. She advanced to the fourth rounds at the "Sunshine Double" (Indian Wells Open and Miami Open), rising to a career-high singles ranking of World No. 29. Eala plays from the baseline and likes to attack with her shots. As a lefty, she uses her strong forehand and steady two‑handed backhand to control rallies. Her returns are good because she adds topspin and reads the ball well. Her serve is weaker since it is not very fast or varied. Coaches say she should work on adding more power, staying consistent, thinking of more tactics, and improving her fitness. She won bronze medals at the 2021 Southeast Asian Games and the 2022 Asian Games, helped the Philippines gain promotion in the 2024 Billie Jean King Cup, and won gold in singles at the 2025 Southeast Asian Games. Eala began endorsing Globe Telecom at age eight and has since partnered with Babolat, Nike, the Bank of the Philippine Islands, and became a Milo brand ambassador. She has won several Philippine Sportswriters Association awards. In 2021, Tatler Asia listed her as one of Asia’s most influential people.

Alexandre Bolduc (born June 26, 1985 in Montreal, Quebec) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre who currently plays for the Arizona Coyotes of the National Hockey League (NHL). Bolduc was selected by the St. Louis Blues with the 127th pick in the 2004 NHL Draft but never played for them. He has also played for the Vancouver Canucks. He signed a contract with the Coyotes on July 2, 2011.
Alexandre Paes Lopes (born 29 October 1974) is a Brazilian professional athlete. He is best known as a football player. He has played for Brazil national team.
Alexandre Rodrigues da Silva (born 2 September 1989), better known as Alexandre Pato, is a Brazilian football former player, who played as a striker. He is currently a sports commentator on SBT.

Alexandre Bilodeau (born September 8, 1987 in Montreal, Quebec) is a Canadian retired freestyle skier. He skied in the men's moguls events for Canada at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver. He won the gold medal at the 2010 Games and became the first Canadian to win a gold medal at an Olympic Games held in Canada. Bilodeau also competed at the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi where he successfully defended his gold medal and became the first Canadian to defend an individual title since Catriona Lemay Doan at the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City. He has also won FIS World Championships in dual moguls. On March 21, 2014, Bilodeau said that he was going to retire after the 2013–14 FIS Freestyle Skiing World Cup season.

Alexandre Gaiscoigne (born 20 September 1989) is a South African water polo player. She competed for the South Africa women's national water polo team in the 2015 World Aquatics Championships. She studied at University of Pretoria.
Alexandre Kalache is a volleyball player from Brazil. Alexandre competed at the 1972 Summer Olympics and the 1976 Summer Olympics. He was born on 28 February 1952.

Alexandre Texier (born 13 September 1999) is a French professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Columbus Blue Jackets and St. Louis Blues. Outside of the NHL, Texier played for the Brûleurs de Loups of the Ligue Magnus, KalPa of the Liiga, and the ZSC Lions of the National League (NL). Texier was the winner of the Jean-Pierre Graff Trophy in 2017. Before playing in the NHL, Texier played parts of one season with the Brûleurs de Loups of the Ligue Magnus. He had a successful time with them. He was awarded the Jean-Pierre Graff Trophy for being the most promising player of that year. He also won the Coupe de France with them that year as well. He was drafted 45th overall by the Columbus Blue Jackets in the 2017 NHL entry draft, making him the first ever French player to be drafted into the NHL directly out of France. On 22 May 2018, Texier signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Blue Jackets. On 5 April 2019, Texier made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime win against the New York Rangers. The next day, he scored his first NHL goal against Anders Nilsson in a 6–2 win against the Ottawa Senators. On 28 July 2021, Texier signed a two-year contract to stay with the Blue Jackets. On 28 June 2024, the Blue Jackets traded Texier to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for a 2025 fourth-round draft pick. He played 39 regular season games over two seasons with the Blues. On 22 November 2025, the Blues placed Texier onto waivers and they terminated his contract. On 23 November 2025, Texier signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Montreal Canadiens. On 8 January 2026, Texier recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–2 win against the Florida Panthers. On 14 January, Texier signed a two-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Canadiens.
Alexei Valeryevich Yashin (; born November 5, 1973) is a former Russian professional ice hockey player. Yashin played in the NHL for the Ottawa Senators and the New York Islanders.

Oleksiy Volodymyrovych "Alexei" Ponikarovsky (born 9 April 1980 in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union) is a Ukrainian-Canadian former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 15 season in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Toronto Maple Leafs, Pittsburgh Penguins, Los Angeles Kings, Carolina Hurricanes, New Jersey Devils, and Winnipeg Jets. He also played in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL) for Donbass Donetsk, SKA Saint Petersburg, and Kunlun Red Star. He was drafted by the Toronto Maple Leafs with the 87th overall pick in the 1998 NHL Entry Draft. He also played in the NHL for the Toronto Maple Leafs for 9 seasons, the Pittsburgh Penguins for 1 season, the Los Angeles Kings for 1 season, the Carolina Hurricanes for 1 season, the New Jersey Devils for 1 season and the Winnipeg Jets for 1 season. He was traded back to the Devils on February 13, 2013 in exchange for a 4th round pick and a 7th round pick in the 2014 NHL Entry Draft. He is nicknamed "The Poni Express", "The Ukraine Train" and "Poni". He currently lives in Toronto with his wife Inna, daughter Jessica, and sons Alex and Maxim. He also became a Canadian citizen on June 7, 2007. In the 1998 NHL Draft, he was selected in round 4 under a total of 87 by the Toronto Maple Leafs. Has Canadian and Russian citizenship. In 2010 he was traded to the Pittsburgh Penguins. In the summer of 2010, as a free agent, he signed a contract with the Los Angeles Kings for a period of 1 year. In the summer of 2011, he changed Los Angeles to Carolina Hurricanes, signing a one-year agreement worth $ 1.5 million. In January 2012, before the expiration of his contract, he was traded to the New Jersey Devils. In the offseason 2012, signed a one-year contract with the Winnipeg Jets for $ 1.5 million Due to the NHL lockout in 2012, he signed a contract with the newcomer of the KHL, the Donbass club. After the end of the lockout he returned to the Winnipeg Jets, but after 12 games on 14 February 2013 he returned to the New Jersey Devils. In August 2016, he signed a contract with the Kunlun Red Star Kontinental Hockey League debut. In November 2017, he joined the Putin Team movement Married. He has three children.

Alexei Pavlovich Tezikov (; June 22, 1978 – July 16, 2020) was a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He played in the National Hockey League with the Washington Capitals and Vancouver Canucks. Tezikov left North America following the 2001–02 season, returning to his native Russia to play in the Russian Superleague and Kontinental Hockey League over the next 11 years. Tezikov died on July 16, 2020, at the age of 42, after suffering a heart attack on the street.
Alexandru Bădiţă is a retired water polo player from Romania. Bădiţă competed at the 1956 Summer Olympics and the 1960 Summer Olympics. He was born on 2 October 1937.

Alexei Vyacheslavovich Emelin (born 25 April 1986) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He is currently an unrestricted free agent. He played parts of seven seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Montreal Canadiens and Nashville Predators. He also played for Lada Togliatti, Ak Bars Kazan, Avangard Omsk, Dinamo Minsk, and Spartak Moscow of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Emelin played three seasons with Lada Togliatti of the Russian Superleague (RSL) and four seasons with Ak Bars Kazan of the RSL/Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 84th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 2004 NHL entry draft. On 17 May 2011, Emelin signed a one-year, two-way contract to join the Montreal Canadiens. On 9 October, Emelin made his NHL debut in a 5–1 win against the Winnipeg Jets. On 6 December, Emelin recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Brian Gionta goal in a 3-2 shootout loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets. On January 25, 2012, Emelin scored is first NHL goal in a 7-2 win against the Detroit Red Wings. On 30 June, Emelin signed a two-year extension to stay with the Canadiens. On 6 April 2013, Emelin's season ended after he suffered a torn ligament in his left knee when he landed awkwardly on the ice from a hit by Bruins forward Milan Lucic. On 31 October, Emelin signed a four-year contract extension to stay with the Canadiens. On 21 June 2017, the Canadiens allowed Emelin to be selected by the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2017 NHL expansion draft but he did not play a game for them. On 1 July, the Golden Knights traded Emelin to the Nashville Predators in exchange for a 2019 third-round pick. He played 76 games with the Predators and scored one goal. On 2 September 2018, Emelin returned to Russia after signing a three-year contract with Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He played parts of four seasons with the team. on 26 July 2022, Emelin signed a one-year contract to join Dinamo Minsk. He was selected to represent the team as their captain and played 38 games with them.

Alexei Yuryevich Zhamnov (born October 1, 1970 in Moscow, URS) is a Russian retired professional ice hockey centre. He is currently the head coach for the KHL's Vityaz Chekhov. Zhamnov played a combined 14 seasons in the NHL with four teams, 4 while part of the Winnipeg Jets, 8 while part of the Chicago Blackhawks, 1 while part of the Philadelphia Flyers and 1 while part of the Boston Bruins. Zhamnov was also the captain of the Chicago Blackhawks from 2002-2004.

In January 2018, he joined The Red Devils after Henrikh Mkhitaryan swapped clubs with him to Arsenal FC. Alexey Arhipovsky (; May 15, 1967) – is a Russian balalaika virtuoso player. He was born in the town of Tuapse, Krasnodar Territory, Russia on May 15, 1967. His father played the garmon and accordion. At the age of 9, Arhipovsky started at musical school to study the balalaika. Later he entered Gnessin State Musical College, the department of folk instruments, class – balalaika. Upon graduation, he entered the Smolensk folk orchestra as a soloist-balalaika. In 1985 he became a laureate of the Contest of Folk Instrument Performers in Russia. Since 1998 he toured around Russia and abroad with the State Academic Folk Ensemble "Rossiya" Russia directed by Lyudmila Zykina. Since 2002 he cooperated with Stas Namin, the musician, composer, and record producer. Arhipovsky took part in festivals of Russian culture in the United States, China, South Korea, Germany, France, Spain and Bulgaria. He participated in jazz festivals in Russia and abroad, in radio and TV programmes. During his tours, fans compared his performance with Paganini and Jimi Hendrix. Critics have dubbed him the “Paganini of the Russian balalaika”. He recorded a DVD album Alexey Arhipovsky in 2009. In 2009, he was invited to participate in the opening ceremony of the second semi-final of the Eurovision song contest in Moscow.

Alexis Shifflett is an American sitting volleyball player. She played at the 2016 Summer Paralympics, winning a gold medal, 2014 ParaVolley World Championships, 2018 ParaVolley World Championships, and 2019 Parapan American Games. She was born in Owatonna, Minnesota. She studied at Waseca Junior and Senior High School in Waseca, Minnesota.

Alexia Putellas Segura (born 4 February 1994) is a Catalan professional footballer. She plays as a midfielder for Barcelona, whom she captains, and for the Spain women's national football team. Before this, she played for Espanyol and Levante, and she has represented Catalonia. By 2022, she had won all the major awards available to a European player, both individually and with her club. People widely consider her the best female footballer in the world right now and one of the greatest of all time. In 2022, a football reporter named Asif Burhan mentioned how her dedication to the sport has changed women's football. She has been playing for Barcelona since 2012, after spending most of her younger years with Espanyol. With Barcelona, she has achieved a lot: seven league titles, seven Copas de la Reina, and two UEFA Women's Champions League trophies. In the 2020-21 season, she played a key role in helping Barcelona win the Champions League and two other major titles for the first time in their history. In recognition of her outstanding performance, she won several awards in 2021, including UEFA Women's Player of the Year, Ballon d'Or Féminin, and The Best FIFA Women's Player - a feat that no one had accomplished before in a single year. As of 2022, she's the second player with the most appearances for Barcelona, just behind Melanie Serrano. She's also the second-highest all-time scorer for the club, after Jennifer Hermoso. Moreover, she holds the record for the most appearances for Spain with 104 caps, surpassing Marta Torrejón's previous record of 90 caps in 2021. Putellas was really close to her dad. Even though he was sick with heart problems when she played for Levante, he always came to see her games in Valencia. She thought about studying medicine to help him. He died in 2012, just before an important tournament. When she scores a goal, she points to the sky to remember him. She mostly speaks Catalan, learned Spanish in school when she was young, and started learning English in the 2020s. She has a pet dog named Nala, a Pomeranian, who even has an Instagram account. She doesn't talk much about her relationships, but she did share on social media about being with her teammate Jennifer Hermoso. They even joined an event called Madrid Pride together. After winning the Champions League in 2023, a video of Putellas meeting her girlfriend in the stands became super popular on TikTok. Putellas has lots of tattoos. Some have Latin sayings, like "Work conquers all." She also has symbols like a Hand of Fatima and an Eye of Horus, plus a Barcelona tile with "Made in" written on it. She's got a football, the number 112 (combining her first Spain shirt number, 12, and her famous shirt number, 11), and a drawing of her dad holding her as a baby and giving her a football. Alexey Leonidovich Toropchenko (; born 25 June 1999) is a Russian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Toropchenko played for the Kunlun Red Star of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Toropchenko played two seasons with the Guelph Storm of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 113th overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2017 NHL entry draft. On 13 December 2018, Toropchenko signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was sent down to their AHL-affiliate San Antonio Rampage. On 5 April 2019, the Blues called him up and Toropchenko made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the Dallas Stars. On 9 February 2022, Toropchenko signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to stay with the Blues. On 19 March 2022, he scored his first NHL goal against Elvis Merzļikins in a 5–4 loss against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On 16 July 2023, Toropchenko signed a two-year, $2.5 million contract to stay with the Blues. On 29 October 2024, Toropchenko signed a one-year, $1.7 million contract to stay with the Blues. Toropchenko's father Leonid was also a professional hockey player who played 14 seasons in the NHL. His father died from a heart attack in May 2017.

Alexis Lafrenière (born October 11, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Lafrenière played one season with the Rimouski Océanic of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Océanic. He was named back-to-back CHL/David Branch Player of the Year Awards. He also won the RDS Cup as rookie of the year, Michel Brière Memorial Trophy as most valuable player, Jean Béliveau Trophy as top scorer, Michel Bergeron Trophy as the top offensive rookie of the year, and back-to-back Paul Dumont Trophys as personality of the year. He was named to the QMJHL All-Rookie Team and back-to-back First All-Star Teams. He was drafted 1st overall by the New York Rangers of the 2020 NHL entry draft. On October 12, 2020, Lafrenière signed an three-year entry-level contract to join the Rangers. On January 14, 2021, Lafrenière made his NHL debut in a 4–0 loss against the New York Islanders. On January 28, Lafrenière scored his first NHL goal against Linus Ullmark in a 3–2 overtime win against the Buffalo Sabres. It was also the overtime-winning goal. On August 24, 2023, Lafrenière signed a two-year, $4.65 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On March 30, 2024, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 8–5 win against the Arizona Coyotes. On October 25, Lafrenière signed a seven-year, $52.15 million contract to stay with the Rangers.

(Sir) Alf Ramsey (22 January 1920 – 28 April 1999) was an English footballer and football manager. He was born in 1920 and played for Southampton F.C. and Tottenham Hotspur F.C. He also played for the England national football team 32 times and scored three goals. Alf Ramsey was in charge of Ipswich Town F.C. for nearly ten years, Ipswich are the only team to win the First Division title in their first season in the top flight the season after winning the second division. Ramsey then became manager of the England team. He was manager when England beat Germany 4–2 in the World Cup final at Wembley Stadium. He is the only England manager to win a World Cup. In recognition of his achievement in leading England to victory in the World Cup Alf Ramsey was knighted in 1967. He died of a heart attack. In tribute to Ramsey, Ipswich Town F.C. commissioned a life-size statue of him which is positioned directly in front of Portman Road (home ground of Ipswich Town F.C.).

Alf Handrahan (born December 27, 1949) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey player. He played in the World Hockey Association. He played fourteen games for the Cincinnati Stingers. He was born in Alberton, Prince Edward Island.

Alexis Alain Vastine (17 November 1986 – 9 March 2015) was a French boxer. He won a bronze medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics in the Light Welterweight division. He also competed in the 2012 Summer Olympics. He died in the Villa Castelli helicopter crash during the filming of French TV reality show Dropped for the TF1 network.

Aleš Kotalík (born 23 December 1978) is a Czech former professional ice hockey right winger. He played a total of nine seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres, Edmonton Oilers, New York Rangers, and Calgary Flames. He also played for HC České Budějovice and HC Bílí Tygři Liberec in the Czech Extraliga (ELH). Before playing in the NHL, Kotalík played four seasons with HC České Budějovice of the Czech Extraliga (ELH). He was drafted 164th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 1998 NHL entry draft. He spent time playing between the Sabres and their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On November 12, 2001, the Sabres called Kotalík up and he made his NHL debut in a 5-3 win against the Florida Panthers. During the game, he recorded his first point in the NHL when he assisted on a Curtis Brown goal. On March 19, 2002, he recorded his first goal in the NHL in a 5-1 win against the Ottawa Senators. He went on to play parts of seven seasons with the Sabres. On 4 March 2009, the Sabres traded Kotalík to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for a 2009 second round pick. He finished the season with them and played 19 games, scoring 7 goals and 4 assists. On 9 July, Kotalík signed a three-year, $9 million contract to join the New York Rangers. He played 45 games with the Rangers before being scratched because of poor performance. On 1 February 2010, the Rangers traded Kotalík along with Chris Higgins to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Olli Jokinen and Brandon Prust. He played 52 games over two seasons with the Flames before they waived him and he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Abbotsford Heat. He played 25 games with the Heat. On 25 June, the Flames traded Kotalík along with Robyn Regehr and a 2012 second round pick to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for Paul Byron and Chris Butler. On 24 September 2011, the Sabres placed him on waivers. Kotalík instead decided to return to the Czech Republic and play for HC České Budějovice again. He played until 2013 and then retired from playing professional ice hockey.

Aleš Hemský (born 13 August 1983) is an Czech former professional ice hockey right winger. He played parts of 15 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Edmonton Oilers, Ottawa Senators, Dallas Stars, and Montreal Canadiens. Outside of the NHL, Hemský played for HC Dynamo Pardubice of the Czech Extraliga (EHL). Hemský is a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2011. Internationally, he played for the Czech Republic national team and won a bronze medal with them at the 2006 Winter Olympics in Turin. Before playing in the NHL, Hemský played parts of two seasons with the Hull Olympiques of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Olympiques, being named to the QMJHL All-Rookie team, the CHL All-Rookie Team, and was awarded the Mike Bossy Trophy for being the best professional prospect in the QMJHL. This came after he finished his rookie season, scoring 36 goals and recording 100 points which led all rookies in the league. He was named to both the QMJHL second All-Star team and CHL third All-Star team the next season. He was drafted 13th overall by the Edmonton Oilers in the 2001 NHL entry draft. On 10 October 2002, Hemský made his NHL debut in a 2–2 overtime tie against the Philadelphia Flyers. On 12 October 2002, he recorded his first career point, assisting on a Mike Comrie goal in a 2–2 overtime tie against the Nashville Predators. On 4 January 2003, Hemský scored his first NHL career goal against José Théodore in a 5–4 overtime win against the Montreal Canadiens. He helped the Oilers during the playoffs. They defeated the Detroit Red Wings, San Jose Sharks, and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim. They were eventually defeated by the Carolina Hurricanes four games to three in the Final. On 25 July 2006, Hemský signed a six-year, $24.60 million contract to stay with the Oilers. On 11 January 2011, He was selected to play in the NHL All-Star Game but was unable to and had to be replaced because he was recovering from a concussion. On 24 February 2012, Hemský signed a two-year, $10 million to stay with the Oilers. On 5 March 2014, the Oilers traded Hemský to the Ottawa Senators in exchange for a 2014 fifth-round pick and a 2015 third-round pick. He played 20 games, scoring 4 goals and recording 13 assists. On 1 July 2014, Hemský signed a three-year, $12 million contract to join the Dallas Stars. He played parts of three seasons with the Stars. On 3 July 2017, Hemský signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Montreal Canadiens. He was only able to play 7 games with the team. On 20 October, he was hit twice in a game by Anaheim Ducks players Josh Manson and Corey Perry. This resulted in him having to be helped off the ice and was later diagnosed with a severe concussion. He never played another game in the NHL afterwards. On 15 May 2020, Hemský officially announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Alfred Ernest Moore (December 1, 1904 – June 29, 1979) was a Canadian ice hockey goaltender. Moore played 20 games in the NHL for the New York Americans. Moore is known for replacing Mike Karakas in the Chicago Black Hawks net in game one of the 1938 Stanley Cup Finals because replacement goaltender Paul Goodman did not arrive in Toronto on time. He spent the end of his career in the AHL, playing for the Cleveland Barons, New Haven Eagles, Springfield Indians, Buffalo Bisons and Philadelphia Rockets. In 1941, Moore retired from playing professional ice hockey. In 1949, he became the head coach of the Galt Black Hawks of the Ontario Hockey Association which he coached for 1 season.
